summary: The Meta-Physicist (profession 12) is a pet class that controls up to three simultaneous floating 'manifestation' pets: one Attack pet (damage), one Heal pet (heals owner/team/pets/NPCs/towers), and one Mezz/Support pet (a single-target STUN, not a calm). Attack pets are summoned with Time&Space (131) + Matter Creation (130); Heal pets with Time&Space + Biological Metamorphosis (128); Mezz pets with Time&Space + Matter Metamorphosis (127). Pets are no longer on a timer, so they persist and can be cast over-equipped (wrangled) to run higher-level pets. The MP also has a large library of pet buffs: short-term damage burst (Evocation/Anima, strain 225), long-term pet weapon-skill buffs (Instill, strain 216), initiative buffs (Chant, strain 217), pet defensive/AC and nano-resist buffs (strains 816/817), plus damage-transfer and pet-utility nanos. Ids/names/minLevels below are taken verbatim from metaphysicist-nanos.json (client 18.8.50 extraction); mechanics and 'best pet' guidance are from the cited AO community sources.

petTypes.description: The MP's primary damage dealer and its main weapon for most of the game. Better pets do more damage and (historically) lasted longer; MPs should always run the strongest attack pet their skills (or a wrangle) allow. Froob pets form a continuous Matter-Creation/Time&Space-gated ladder through six 'emotion' families (Anger -> Fury -> Rage -> Wrath -> Frenzy -> Enmity), each with Inferior / base / Superior / Greater / Supreme / Transcendent sub-tiers, topped by Summon Lemur/Fiend/Demon. Shadowlands adds the high-end named pets (Biazu, Urolok, Ettu, Zhok) culminating in The Rihwen at 220.
petTypes.mechanics: Cast the highest pet you qualify for, then command it (attack/guard/behind). Damage is raised further with Instill (216) long-term buffs, Chant (217) initiative buffs, and Evocation/Anima (225) short-term damage bursts, all of which require NPCFamily==97 (i.e. an attack pet) as their target family. Use /oe to verify skill vs pet requirement when over-equipping.

petTypes.description: A dedicated healing manifestation. Casting the first heal pet changes MP gameplay dramatically: it can heal the MP, teammates, other pets, some NPCs, and Notum Wars towers. There are 10 strengths, from Calling of Medinos up to Calling of Mortificant the Eternal (Shadowlands, the strongest).
petTypes.mechanics: Ordered heal target with /pet heal (heals current friendly target). The Soothing Spirit perk (Shadowlands) improves heal-pet output. Each SummonPet event lists the template 7 times (the pet's healing action), consistent across the line.

progression.note: Endgame / best heal pet (Shadowlands only), template 215; BioMet > 1465, TS > 1462, Specialization 8.

petTypes.description: The MP's crowd-control manifestation. It applies a single-target STUN (NOT a calm): the mezzed target cannot move, cast, or attack. Only one target is affected at a time. There are 16-17 versions from Lesser Distracting Sphere up to Summoning of Tumulten, plus the Shadowlands Summoning of Yidira.
petTypes.mechanics: Order the mezz pet onto a target; the pet re-applies its stun. Because it is a stun rather than a calm it can lock a single mob out of all actions. Pet templates below track the mezz pet's level.

progression.note: Endgame / best mezz pet (Shadowlands, Expansion req), template 210; MatMeta/TS > 1297.

mechanics: Three simultaneous pets max: one Attack (strain 1015), one Heal (1016), one Mezz/Support (1017). Casting a second pet of the same line replaces the first.

Summon skills per line: Attack = Time&Space(131)+Matter Creation(130); Heal = Time&Space+Biological Metamorphosis(128); Mezz = Time&Space+Matter Metamorphosis(127). Most older MP pet nanos gate on VisualProfession(368)==12; newer/SL ones on Profession(60)==12.

Pets are no longer on a timer (they used to expire): they persist, so MPs can accept a wrangle/buff to over-equip and summon a pet above their own skill, then let the buff drop. Use /oe to confirm the pet's skill requirement is met at cast time.
The mezz pet applies a single-target STUN, not a calm: the target cannot move, cast, or attack; only one target at a time.
The heal pet can heal the owner, teammates, other pets, some NPCs, and Notum Wars towers - not just the MP.

Attack-pet damage/initiative buffs (Evocation/Anima 225, Instill 216, Chant 217) require the target to be family NPCFamily==97 (an attack pet). Pet defensive/resist buffs (816/817) and heal-delta (843) target the pet directly.
Default pet mode after a cast or a zone is GUARD; convention is to issue /pet behind immediately after zoning so pets don't pull uncontrolled aggro, then /pet attack or /pet guard when ready.
Pet control is per-pet: commands can be scoped to a named pet (rename first) so the attack, heal, and mezz pets can be driven independently from one macro set.

Pet-sacrifice/damage-transfer tools: 'Sacrifice Combat pet' (267533) destroys the attack pet for a large short-term damage buff; 'Sacrificial Bond'/'Sacrificial Shielding' (300506/267281) redirect owner damage to the pet.
Pet recovery: 'Pet Steal Back' (269907) and 'Improved Pet Steal Back' (269908) (Charm_Short strain 1022, RemoveNanoStrain[202]) let the MP reclaim a pet that was charmed/stolen.

Bot note: to pick the strongest castable pet per line, filter metaphysicist-nanos.json by nanoLine (AttackPets/HealPets/SupportPets) and choose the highest SpaceTime/secondary-skill castReq the character's current skills satisfy (auto-detect from live stats), rather than hardcoding a per-level table.
_unverified: Exact character-level breakpoints for froob pets: metaphysicist-nanos.json lists minLevel 0 for nearly all froob pet nanos (the real gate is the nano-skill requirement, not character level). The per-pet 'template ~N' notes are derived from the SummonPet template argument in local data, not from a published level chart - treat as an ordering proxy, not an exact character-level requirement.

Fandom states '16 different versions of the mezz pet'; the local 18.8.50 extract has 17 Mezz/Support nanos (16 pre-SL + Summoning of Yidira). The count discrepancy is likely the SL addition - not independently reconciled.

No pet-WARP nano appears in the MP-castable local extract (NanoLine PetWarp=1019 exists in the enum but no matching MP nano was found). Pet warp as a game mechanic is referenced by sources but its id/availability for MP is unconfirmed here - flag before implementing a warp action.
Pet-buff durations, stacking rules, and whether short-term (Evocation/Anima 225) vs long-term (Instill 216) buffs overwrite each other are not verified against wire data.
Which named SL attack pet is strictly 'best' at 220 (The Rihwen vs a wrangled Zhok) is stated from community consensus/forum guide, not measured.
Soothing Spirit perk boosting heal-pet output is from the Funcom forum guide; exact magnitude not verified.
